subject: MedGuard tenant log TTL & preservation exception — scope and next steps
messages:
From: Ellen Park <ellen.park@medguard.ai>
To: ava.chen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: samir.rao@medguard.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request — tenant-level 90d log preservation for upcoming SOC2 audit

Hi Ava,

Quick note from procurement/security at MedGuard — we have a SOC 2 Type II readiness audit scheduled for the week of 2028-07-04, and our auditor has requested that we provide 90 days of tenant-scoped request/trace logs for a handful of test users.

Your standard product TTL (30d ephemeral debug traces) was fine during evaluation, but the auditor is now asking for a retention exception for a single tenant to validate incident response and access trails. Can Redwood provide: an export of request/log traces for the tenant for the 90d window, a short statement describing the deletion workflow, and any CAIQ/SIG evidence that maps to how tenant logs are stored/erased?

We realize this is outside the default contract. Please advise whether a temporary preservation window or a tenant-level exception is feasible, and what the timeline and expected deliverables would be. Procurement is trying to avoid contract redlines if possible.

Thanks,
Ellen Park
Director, IT Compliance — MedGuard AI

(attachment: auditor_request_summary.pdf)
From: ava.chen@redwoodinference.com
To: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ellen.park@medguard.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — tenant-level 90d log preservation for upcoming SOC2 audit

Thanks Ellen — looping in SRE (Priyom), Security (Irene) and Sales (Ben) so we can scope. High-level: we can take a targeted preservation approach for a tenant, but we need to confirm storage, retention mechanics (KV cache vs. request traces), and whether this is a hold (prevent deletion) or a copy/export.

Priyom — can you confirm technical feasibility for a 90d retention for a single tenant and whether we can generate a CSV export of request traces spanning 90 days? What are the runtime/storage implications and ETA to produce the export?

Irene — MedGuard specifically asked for CAIQ/SIG evidence mapping — do we have an existing evidence pack that covers log lifecycle and deletion controls we can share, or do we need to assemble a tailored narrative?

Ben — procurement prefers not to redline. If an addendum is required (one-off tenant retention), what commercial options (credit/one-time fee) should we propose?

Goal: provide MedGuard with a clear list of deliverables and a timeline within 3 business days.

— Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com
To: ava.chen@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ellen.park@medguard.ai
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 11:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — tenant-level 90d log preservation for upcoming SOC2 audit

On Tue, Jun 5, 2028 at 10:03 AM ava.chen@redwoodinference.com wrote:
> Priyom — can you confirm technical feasibility for a 90d retention for a single tenant and whether we can generate a CSV export of request traces spanning 90 days?

Short answer: feasible, with caveats.

Plan and items we'll deliver if approved:
- Scoped preservation: create a tenant-level retention policy that marks the tenant's request traces immutable for 90 days (preserve-on-write). This is implemented as a short-term retention flag in our logging service, not a global config change.
- Export: produce a compressed CSV export (tenant_log_export_90d.csv.gz) with the requested fields (timestamp, request_id, route, user_id hash, latency_ms, outcome, node_id). Export generation ETA: ~4 business days after approval.
- Deletion evidence: a short playbook (deletion_playbook.pdf) describing how deletion jobs are scheduled, KMS/HSM key rotations, and a sample 'proof of delete' procedure we run at TTL expiry.
- Artifact alignment: map fields to CAIQ/SIG assertions; we can pull the standard SIG pack and add a one-page mapping for tenant log lifecycle.

Resource/cost note: the preservation flag will increase retained data for that tenant for the 90d window. For a medium activity tenant this is ~60GB additional storage for 90d; approximate incremental cost (storage + egress for export) we should price with Sales.

Blocking items: legal addendum sign-off for a tenant-level deviation from default TTLs (we need a one-time addendum that specifies scope/duration). Also need MedGuard to confirm the exact tenant IDs and the audit window.

Irene, will need sec review of the evidence text. Ben, if we run a one-time export + short preservation period what level of commercial arrangement do you want to propose?

— Priyom Das
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
To: ava.chen@redwoodinference.com, priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com
Cc: ellen.park@medguard.ai
Date: Wed, 6 Jun 2028 08:16:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — tenant-level 90d log preservation for upcoming SOC2 audit

Thanks team. From a commercial perspective:
- For a one-off preservation + export we should offer a standard fee (to cover storage and engineering time) but be prepared to offer a small onboarding credit to avoid contract redlines.
- Suggest we propose: $1,800 one-time fee + 3% of estimated incremental monthly storage (prorated) OR a one-time credit of $1,500 if MedGuard signs the addendum within 5 business days.
- I'll coordinate with Legal to get a minimal addendum template. Irene — once you sign off on the security narrative we can attach it as Exhibit A to the addendum.

Ellen — if this commercial approach works we can fast-track legal and production scope. Please confirm tenant IDs and whether the auditor needs the raw export or a filtered/sanitized version (we can hash PII fields).

— Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
From: ava.chen@redwoodinference.com
To: ellen.park@medguard.ai
Cc: priyom.das@redwoodinference.com, irene.choi@redwoodinference.com, ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 7 Jun 2028 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request — tenant-level 90d log preservation for upcoming SOC2 audit (next steps)

Ellen — thanks for the quick turnaround. Confirming next steps and timeline: 

1) MedGuard confirms tenant IDs and whether PII should be hashed or fully redacted (reply by EOD 2028-06-08 preferred).
2) Redwood will provision a tenant-level 90d preservation flag (not global) and run the export once the window is ready. ETA for export: 4 business days after provisioning (we'll schedule provisioning within 1 business day after your confirmation).
3) Deliverables: tenant_log_export_90d.csv.gz (stub), deletion_playbook.pdf (security narrative for CAIQ/SIG alignment), and an SLA addendum template (sla_addendum_template.docx).
4) Commercials: Ben proposes the fee/credit options above; we will await MedGuard's preference.
5) Legal addendum: Redwood Legal will prepare a one-page addendum; Irene will be the internal security sign-off and will attach Exhibit A (evidence mapping).

If that timeline works for you we'll treat this as a scoped tenant exception (no platform-wide TTL change) and move to legal.

Please reply to confirm tenant IDs and acceptance of the above approach.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
(attachment stubs to follow: tenant_log_export_90d.csv, deletion_playbook.pdf, sla_addendum_template.docx)
